angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 382,635 km at 33.01 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 30.2902 +/- 0.0295 mas (same row, RUWE 1.39): 33.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.55 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Reefe et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-620 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..269R/abstract): 382,635 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.577 +/- 0.024 solar masses from Reefe et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-620 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..269R/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3708 +/- 57 K from Reefe et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-620 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..269R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Reefe et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-620 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..269R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-620.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.719, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
